set.approach: Leave the car beside the road above the Wilderness Permit Center, or use that center's lot. Begin just east of the turnoff to the permit center and Tuolumne Lodge and head north, uphill; a good trail begins a short way in but can be hard to spot the first time. The wall is east-facing and the first climbs come up after a short uphill walk, with the far end a little farther on. Alive at Leads climbs broken flakes to a single bolt on the slab above.

set.approach: The Entrance Boulder is just north of the south parking area at the Pinnacles: walk north along the side road a short way before you reach the lot. Its climbs face northwest. Not That Crack starts below and left of Short Stack and follows a left-slanting offwidth crack.

review.notes: Route + area.

set.approach: The Fins are a set of narrow pinnacles west of the Hungover Wall and Shirtsleeve Rock, both reached from Keller Peak Road. From the Shirtsleeve Rock area go up and over the north-facing rocks, then drop down to the visible pinnacles. The route is a thin, awkward left-facing corner crack in the inside corner right of the route Otto.

review.notes: Route + area pages.

set.approach: Drive Forest Road 2N86 to its end and walk south to the obvious boulder, across the road from Castle Grey Skull; the walk takes only a few minutes. The route is on the west face and laybacks a left-leaning, left-facing flake before face climbing past a bolt to the top.

review.notes: Route + area.

set.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, an old road and then a trail lead to Lower Pine Lake. Go beyond Upper Pine Lake, but turn left before reaching Honeymoon Lake and cross Pine Creek Pass and drop into French Canyon. Where the first big waterfall tumbles down on the right from Merriam Peak's flanks, you reach the wall. The route climbs beside the waterfall, up a right-facing dihedral that turns into an arete.

review.notes: Route + area; no descent stated.

set.approach: The Gill Face is a short walk past the fence line at the south side of Holcomb Valley Pinnacles. John Gill is the single route on the left side of the face, on a south-facing block split by horizontal cracks, left of the route New Pygmy.

review.notes: Route + area; thin access source.

set.approach: Take Gleason Ranch Road to the point beneath the rock and walk up from there; the other option is to come in from the east off Highway 178. The only route on the pyramid-shaped peak's north face begins in a fourth-class slot chimney.

review.notes: Route + area.

set.approach: The route is on a small band of south-facing cliffs at the junction of Gleason Ranch Road and Highway 178, just west of the Chimney Peak Road junction. It takes the longest, least broken face: from the boulders below, start on the right side of the face and climb to a bolt, then cross left on a dike to an arete.

review.notes: Route + area.

set.approach: Use the Mayfield Canyon approach on the Wheeler Crest, to the Grey Towers behind the Pink Band; there is no trail. The Zebra Slab is tucked behind Hot Tuna Tower, under an unnamed grey tower. Blackout follows the vertical black dike that stands out in the middle of the slab among horizontal white dikes.
set.descent_text: When the slab gives way to a featured rocky gully above you, go down on the climber's right, following the fourth-class gully to the dirt. The gully can be reached by descending the back side of Hot Tuna Tower.

review.notes: Route page: descent; area page: approach.

set.approach: Grouse Tor is the rounded summit east of the Grouse Ridge lookout; an easy walk from the parking area before the campground leads to the top, and a north-facing wall sits above Sanford Lake. Look for it at the rear of the big plateau high on the right side of the wall: after topping out Corn Silk, look right for a lone bleached pine in the talus field; the route is on the slab behind that tree. Another way to reach the plateau is to scramble down onto it from the face's west side.

review.notes: Route + area; no descent stated for the whole route.

set.approach: Walk from the parking spot to the first mini-crag, the Shooting Gallery, then wind down the canyon to the next crag, Gunslinger Rock, with its climbs on your left. Gym Climb is the face just left of the obvious crack on the west face.
set.descent_text: There are no fixed anchors, so downclimb.

review.notes: Route page: downclimb.

set.approach: Preferred approach: from the small parking area at the end of the dirt road above the condos below the Sherwins, climb straight up the slope to the hiking trail, turn left to the Mammoth Rock trail, then leave the trail toward the rock. Take a clear shelf toward the big golden talus field and follow mixed talus and steep slopes up to the rock. Once in the chute, zigzag one long switchback to the left and then right to reach the wall's foot. Gas Is King is the furthest-right route on the crag.

review.notes: Area pages + route.
